testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, what does it mean if you see no spray from other vehicles?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is stuck under the vehicle.
The tires have soaked up all the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicles are not spraying water, ice has formed. Drive carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: If you transport 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer, what is the minimum number of tie-downs you need?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, even for small cargo.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn drivers behind you that you are driving slowly. Check local laws about using flashers.

questions.question: On a vehicle with air brakes, how should the air compressor drive belt be before each drive?
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: If a tire fails while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can make you lose control. Stay off the brake unless you are about to hit something. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from forming in the air brake system. Check and refill it every day in cold weather.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel from seeing a hazard until you press the brake
The distance traveled from when a hazard appears until you see it
The distance you travel before you decide to brake
The distance you travel from pressing the brake until the vehicle stops

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel from seeing a hazard until you press the brake
questions.explanation: Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels between the moment you see a hazard and the moment you press the brake pedal.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS stops working?

options.text: Press the brake pedal down as hard as possible.

questions.explanation: ABS helps prevent your brakes from locking up during hard braking. If ABS fails, your regular brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Press the brake pedal all the way down and release. If it does not return to normal position, there may be a problem.
Press the brake pedal and release. If you hear a squeak, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when you press the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times and press hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another brake problem.

questions.question: How much water on the road surface is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water. It can happen with just a small amount of water on the road.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you can exit your vehicle to check its position only one time.

questions.question: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving is:

options.text: Allowed for drivers age 18 and older.
Allowed for drivers age 21 and older.
Allowed for drivers age 25 and older.

questions.explanation: In Illinois, you cannot use a hand-held cell phone or other communication device while driving.

questions.question: When inspecting brakes, make sure your brake pads are:
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, check for cracked drums, worn pads, and pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them. Brake pads should be clean and free of these substances.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the truck is not overloaded.
Make sure the cargo is balanced.
Make sure the cargo is secured properly.
Place breakable items under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place breakable items under heavier items.
questions.explanation: When inspecting cargo, check that it is properly secured, balanced, and does not exceed weight limits. Do not place breakable items under heavier items.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is needed:

options.text: When transporting both liquids and gases.
As an option when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: When transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You must have a tank endorsement to transport liquids or gases. This applies to both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:
questions.explanation: Distracted driving includes physical distractions (like reaching for an object) and mental distractions (like talking to a passenger). It can also include both at the same time (like texting on a phone).

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, what is the maximum air loss allowed during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi of pressure in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: An applicant will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if they:
questions.explanation: An application for a hazardous materials endorsement can be denied if the applicant is wanted for, under indictment for, or convicted of certain felonies. Other reasons include not having legal permanent status in the U.S., renouncing citizenship, being judged mentally incompetent, or being deemed a security threat.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space ahead of your vehicle so they can pass safely. Driving faster will not help because the driver may continue to tailgate at the higher speed, which is dangerous.

questions.question: What information must intrastate carriers display on both sides of their vehicle?

options.text: The model number of the truck

questions.explanation: Vehicles used for intrastate commerce must display the carrier's trade name, permit number, and registration number on both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, you should NOT:

options.text: Turn off the signal after completing the turn.
Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.
questions.explanation: Signal early before turning or changing lanes. Keep the signal on while you complete the turn or lane change. Then turn off the signal so other drivers are not confused.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo can:

options.text: Hurt the driver during a sudden stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurt the driver during a sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be loaded and secured properly. If cargo shifts or falls during a sudden stop, it can injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of the vehicle and its cargo.
The total weight of the vehicle without cargo.
The total weight of the cargo only.
The maximum weight a vehicle is allowed to carry.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the combined weight of the vehicle plus everything it is carrying.

questions.question: Air pressure in a dual air brake system should build from 85 to 100 psi in:
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with dual air brakes, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: A danger when a large truck swerves to avoid a hazard is:

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.
Other vehicles may do the same thing.

questions.explanation: Turning away from a hazard is sometimes better than stopping. You can turn faster than you can stop. But a top-heavy vehicle or one pulling multiple trailers can roll over when swerving.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down and downshift before entering a curve.

questions.question: How many license plates must a truck tractor display?
questions.explanation: Most vehicles must display license plates on the front and back. Truck tractors must display one plate on the front.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Getting a full night's sleep before driving.
Traveling with a passenger you can take turns driving with.
Scheduling trips for times when you are normally asleep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scheduling trips for times when you are normally asleep.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before driving, take turns with a passenger, schedule trips during hours when you are awake, and avoid medications that cause drowsiness.

questions.question: Sending text messages while driving:

options.text: Is allowed if the messages are short.
Is allowed if you are texting your employer.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is prohibited.

questions.question: If you are unfamiliar with an area where you must back up, you should:

options.text: Get out of your vehicle and walk around to learn the area.
Not use both mirrors because it causes too much distraction.
Wait for someone else to back up there first.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of your vehicle and walk around to learn the area.
questions.explanation: Backing is always risky because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you do not know the area, get out and walk around to see your path before backing up.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should the driver do?

options.text: Keep one hand on the steering wheel and wave to other drivers with the other hand.

questions.explanation: If a tire fails, braking can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes unless you must brake to avoid a crash. Let your vehicle slow down on its own. Then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: A 10-foot-long load must be secured with at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers and trailers without sides must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. But always use at least two tie-downs, no matter how small the cargo is.

questions.question: How often must a truck weighing more than 8,000 pounds be inspected?
questions.explanation: Trucks that weigh more than 8,000 pounds must be inspected twice a year for safety.

questions.question: When backing into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive directly into the alley parking space.
Turn right to position yourself in front of the alley.
Drive past the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer boundary.
Drive past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: First, drive past the alley and stop your vehicle parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area. Your vehicle should be parked straight within the parking space lines.

questions.question: When driving through a curve on the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Do not look for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Slow down enough so you do not need to brake or shift gears while turning. Keep your vehicle in its lane and watch for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which of these should you NOT do when checking the oil?

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that the oil level is in a safe range.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the oil dipstick is, show that the oil level is safe, and show that the oil level is above the refill mark. You should NOT show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a truck's cab because of:

options.text: Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It allows poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light turns on, what should you do?

options.text: Drive with one foot on the accelerator and one foot on the brake.
Safely leave the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely leave the road and stop.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop your vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: When should parking brakes be tested?

options.text: Only after you have driven some distance.

questions.explanation: Test your parking brakes before you drive. This is part of your pre-trip inspection. If the parking brakes do not hold, the vehicle needs to be fixed before you drive it.

questions.question: Brake pads should:

options.text: Not have any oil or grease on them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not have any oil or grease on them.
questions.explanation: Brake pads and shoes must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them. Check them during your vehicle inspection.

questions.question: If wheel bearing seals are leaking, you should:

options.text: Add more grease until the seal seems full.
Add brake fluid to the bearing.

questions.explanation: Leaking wheel bearing seals are unsafe. Fix any unsafe problems you find. It is against federal and state law to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on how fast you are going, your vehicle's weight, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only after the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.
Have heaters to prevent them from freezing.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular roads. Drive carefully when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the driver doesn't see you.
Wait for the other driver to signal that it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians cannot see you. This keeps you safe when passing.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Place as little weight as possible over the axles.
Place an appropriate amount of weight over the axles.
Not be concerned about how the weight is distributed.
Only place weight over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place an appropriate amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Balance cargo weight evenly in the trailer. Too much or too little weight on an axle can make the vehicle hard to control and can damage the axle.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass, or change lanes while crossing railroad tracks. Stay in your lane until completely past the crossing.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is thin, clear ice on a road. You can see the road through it, so it may look wet instead of icy. Be very careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: While driving, if a vehicle's ABS is not working, the driver should:

options.text: Use their parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: If the ABS is not working, the regular brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tank.
Are used to drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are used to drain water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and oil. Do this at the end of each driving day to prevent damage.
